subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-communicable disease?
questions.explain: Cardiovascular disease is not caused by a pathogen and cannot be passed between people, so it is non-communicable.

questions.q: Malaria is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explain: Malaria is caused by the protist Plasmodium, spread by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.q: Cholera is caused by which type of pathogen?
questions.explain: Cholera is a bacterial disease that causes severe watery diarrhoea.

questions.q: HIV is an example of which type of pathogen?
questions.explain: HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and can lead to AIDS.

questions.q: Stomach ulcers can be caused by the bacterium known as:
questions.explain: The bacterium Helicobacter pylori infects the stomach lining and can cause ulcers.

questions.q: Which type of white blood cell produces antibodies?
questions.explain: Lymphocytes produce specific antibodies against antigens on a pathogen.

questions.q: The painkiller aspirin was originally derived from which plant?
questions.explain: Aspirin was developed from a chemical (salicylic acid) originally found in willow bark.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, which is produced by which organism?
questions.explain: Fleming discovered that the Penicillium mould produced a substance (penicillin) that killed bacteria.

questions.q: What best describes a communicable disease?
options: A disease caused only by a poor diet
A disease that can be spread between organisms
A disease that is always inherited
A disease that cannot be passed on
questions.explain: Communicable diseases are caused by pathogens that can be transmitted from one organism to another.

questions.q: A vaccine typically works by introducing into the body:
options: Large numbers of active, living pathogens
Small amounts of dead or inactivated pathogen
questions.explain: Dead or inactivated pathogen carries antigens that trigger the immune response without causing disease.

questions.q: Antibodies produced by lymphocytes work by binding to which part of a pathogen?
questions.explain: Antibodies are specific to the antigens on a pathogen's surface, marking it for destruction.

questions.q: Why are antibiotics not used to treat influenza (flu)?
options: Flu is caused by a virus, which antibiotics do not kill
Flu is caused by a fungus that is resistant
questions.explain: Antibiotics kill bacteria but have no effect on viruses, which live inside the body's own cells.

questions.q: Malaria is described as a vector-borne disease because it is spread by:
options: Female mosquitoes that carry the pathogen
questions.explain: The mosquito acts as a vector, transferring the Plasmodium protist between people when it feeds on blood.

questions.q: How does the skin help defend the body against pathogens?
options: It acts as a physical barrier
questions.explain: Unbroken skin forms a physical barrier that stops pathogens entering the body.

questions.q: Studies show a strong correlation between smoking and which non-communicable condition?
questions.explain: Smoking is a major risk factor correlated with increased rates of cardiovascular and lung disease.

questions.q: During preclinical testing, a new medicine is first tested on:
questions.explain: Preclinical trials use cells, tissues and animals to check for toxicity and efficacy before human testing.

questions.q: Using BMI = mass (kg) / height (m)^2, calculate the BMI of a person with mass 81 kg and height 1.8 m.
In a trial, neither the patients nor the doctors know who receives the real drug or the placebo. This design is called a:
questions.explain: A double-blind trial prevents bias because neither patient nor doctor knows who receives the active drug.

questions.q: A person who has recovered from a disease fights off the same pathogen much faster the second time. This is because they now have:
questions.explain: Memory lymphocytes remain after infection and quickly produce the correct antibodies on re-exposure.

questions.q: In a clinical trial, one group of patients is given a pill containing no active drug. This group is used as the:
questions.explain: The placebo group acts as a control so the true effect of the drug can be compared fairly.
